content.text: {"summary":"The Items are thin this window. The clearest builder-relevant change is a vLLM v0.34.0 release-candidate series (rc3 and rc4) touching KV cache connector and test-runner work, though the Items show only truncated titles and no release notes. Modal published two blog posts, one on sandbox resourcing that argues for bursting rather than reserving capacity, and one on a commission and exhibition that is not technical. An arXiv paper proposes optical broadcast memory for datacenter LLM serving as a research direction, not a shipped system.","key_developments":[{"title":"vLLM v0.34.0 release candidates add KV connector and test changes","what_is_new":"vLLM published v0.34.0rc3, whose notes mention allocating an extensible exportable KV cache for KVConnector, and v0.34.0rc4, whose notes mention a release test runner change for warmup gating with speculative decoding. The Items are truncated, so the full scope of each change is not visible.","why_it_matters":"KV cache export and connector work bears on how serving engines move cache state between components, which affects disaggregated serving designs. Speculative decoding test changes suggest ongoing work on that path, but the Items do not confirm user-facing behavior.","sources":["I1","I2"]},{"title":"Modal argues for bursting sandbox capacity instead of reserving it","what_is_new":"Modal's blog post says teams pay for capacity they do not use and describes a way to pay only for what is used, applied to sandbox resourcing. The text is a short summary without implementation details or pricing figures.","why_it_matters":"Burst-based sandbox pricing and scheduling is a competitive position among GPU and compute clouds, relevant to teams running agent or code-execution workloads on managed compute.","sources":["I4"]},{"title":"Optical broadcast memory proposed to remove per-accelerator weight HBM","what_is_new":"An arXiv preprint proposes Optical Broadcast Memory, a hierarchical fiber architecture where a central memory server broadcasts model weights to inference nodes that tap the stream with receive-only co-packaged optics. The authors report, in simulation at 80,000 accelerators, that it eliminates petabytes of HBM while being competitive or better in throughput and energy per token than an HBM-based system, and claim it handles MoE models.","why_it_matters":"If the approach holds, it would change how weights are stored and delivered in serving fleets, with consequences for capacity planning. It is a research proposal, and the Item gives no hardware prototype or independent evaluation.","sources":["I5"]}],"implications":"The vLLM release candidates point to continued engine work on KV cache movement and speculative decoding, which are the kinds of changes that affect serving-cost and latency tradeoffs for builders. Modal's sandbox pricing post signals competition on consumption-based compute models. The optical memory paper is speculative and far from deployment, so it should inform long-range planning only. Given the truncated Items, none of these points can be confirmed beyond the stated claims.","worth_watching":["Full v0.34.0 release notes once final, to confirm what the KVConnector export change does for users","Whether Modal's burst-based sandbox model shows pricing or capacity details in later posts","Independent evaluation or prototypes of the optical broadcast memory design"]}
